title: A newborn and child reportedly died of measles; CDC isn't counting them
gist: New CDC director Erica Schwartz ordered two Pennsylvania measles deaths excluded from the agency's national surveillance data, breaking the precedent that states are the arbiters of case and death determinations, after Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suggested without evidence the state may have fabricated them. The CDC's public death count for 2026 was changed from 0 to 2 and back to an asterisk within roughly 25 hours over one weekend.

insights.claim: The CDC is excluding two measles deaths reported by Pennsylvania health officials from its national measles surveillance update, publicly challenging a state's death determinations and breaking the precedent that states, not the CDC, are the arbiters of case and death determinations.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: If federal surveillance data can be overridden politically, every downstream user of CDC epidemiological data — insurers, pharma, public-health modelers — loses a reference series they had treated as authoritative.
insights.locator: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is excluding

insights.claim: The CDC's measles surveillance page changed three times over one weekend: 2026 total deaths listed as "0" on August 29 at 2:33 pm ET, updated to "2" on August 30 at 12:09 pm ET, then changed again by 3:23 pm ET that day to delete the deaths and replace them with an asterisk.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A documented, timestamped edit trail of a federal data series being revised under political pressure is the kind of evidence that drives litigation and congressional oversight.

insights.claim: New CDC director Erica Schwartz, less than a month into the job, reportedly ordered staff to add an unusual statement to the surveillance page saying available information does not establish whether measles caused or contributed to the deaths.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The directive came from the top of the agency within weeks of appointment, indicating the change is leadership-driven and likely to persist.
insights.quote: At this time, available information does not establish whether measles caused or contributed to the deaths
insights.locator: The New York Times reported Monday

insights.claim: Both people who died were unvaccinated and from Lancaster County, Pennsylvania: one was a newborn and, per Times reporting, the other was a child.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Unvaccinated pediatric deaths in a single county outbreak are the leading indicator of a broader collapse in routine childhood immunization coverage.
insights.locator: But news has since trickled out

insights.claim: Lancaster County Coroner Stephen Diamantoni, a Republican first elected in 2007, said a pathologist determined the newborn died of a ruptured spleen and did not believe measles played a role, even though the baby was born infected with the virus and had evidence of measles infection in lung tissue.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A local elected official's cause-of-death call is being used to override a state health department determination — a new vector for politicizing mortality statistics.

insights.claim: Measles can enlarge a baby's spleen and thin the fibrous tissue around it so the organ can rupture during birth, and after rupture it can be difficult to determine whether the spleen was previously enlarged, according to Paul Offit of Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, who adds that ruptured spleen is extremely rare in newborns.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The mechanism means the coroner's finding is not actually inconsistent with a measles cause — the technical dispute is weaker than the political framing implies.
insights.locator: Measles can cause a baby’s spleen to enlarge

insights.claim: Paul Offit said after contact with state officials that he learned enough about both deaths to conclude "these patients would not have died were it not for measles," and has publicly challenged the coroner to offer an alternative explanation for the ruptured spleen.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Independent expert consensus running against the federal position raises the odds this reverses, but only after the data record has already been damaged.
insights.quote: these patients would not have died were it not for measles

insights.claim: The newborn's Amish parents, who spoke with The Atlantic, said the mother contracted measles during the local outbreak and was so ill she could not speak above a whisper going into labor; the baby was born with a pulse but not breathing and was declared dead less than half an hour later.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The clinical narrative directly contradicts the fabrication insinuation and is the kind of detail that shifts public opinion faster than statistics.

insights.claim: Coroner Diamantoni told The Washington Post he had only recently received information about the second death and his office is still working to determine its cause, leaving unclear on what grounds the state's measles determination was being challenged.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The federal exclusion of the second death rests on no stated evidentiary basis at all, which is the weakest point in the CDC's position.
insights.locator: Far less is publicly known about the second death

insights.claim: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly feuded with Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro over anti-vaccine rhetoric, shared measles misinformation on social media amid news of the deaths, and suggested without evidence that the state may have "fabricated" the deaths and announced them with "giddy delight."
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Cabinet-level attacks on state mortality reporting create direct pressure on the data federal agencies publish, an operating risk for anything downstream of that data.
insights.locator: The move comes after anti-vaccine Health Secretary

insights.claim: The article frames Kennedy's approach as a repeat of the pandemic-era pattern in which he and allies assailed COVID-19 death reports by arguing they were deaths "with" rather than "from" the virus.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The "with versus from" rhetorical template is portable to any disease; expect it applied to future outbreak mortality counts.
insights.locator: Amid the pandemic, Kennedy and like-minded allies

insights.claim: Pennsylvania's health department says it reported the deaths to CDC staff on August 25 before the public announcement and met with CDC officials the next day, contradicting CDC's social media claim that the Governor's Office had not provided relevant information and had declined offers of assistance.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A direct factual conflict between a federal agency and a state health department on the public record is unusual and points to a durable breakdown in outbreak coordination.

insights.claim: Experts had questioned whether new CDC director Schwartz, who has championed vaccine use in the past, would stand up to Kennedy's anti-vaccine agenda, and the decision to challenge Pennsylvania's determinations appears to confirm those fears.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The last institutional check inside the agency has not held, so expect further degradation of federal surveillance reliability rather than a correction.

insights.claim: Former CDC chief medical officer Debra Houry said this is a moment for the CDC director to speak publicly about the outbreak, warning that delays in reporting data further erode trust and create confusion.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Erosion of trust in surveillance data is itself an epidemiological risk factor, raising the probability of larger and costlier future outbreaks.
insights.quote: Delays in reporting of data further erode trust and create confusion.
insights.locator: The CDC’s decision to challenge the death determinations

insights.claim: State health officials initially refused to release information about the two people who died, including their ages, citing privacy concerns, and outside medical experts criticized that opacity for leaving space for doubt and misinformation.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Information vacuums get filled by the loudest actor; transparency speed is now a defensive tool for public-health agencies rather than a courtesy.
